method: Single-session verification under a hard cycle-time constraint (~26 min runway to deadline): primary-source trace via Nvidia's own newsroom press release, cross-checked against independent tech-press pickup (HotHardware) that adds context beyond the release, plus an adversarial search pass for skepticism/non-binding framing. Not the full fresh-verifier-subagent + adversarial-falsifier-subagent split used on other nights -- flagged in the report as a deviation, justified because this is a pure Tier-0 announcement claim type (both companies' own confirmed terms) with low verification burden.
origin_items: Surfaced via Techmeme sweep in this cycle's raw ingest (2026-07-25 gnews/techmeme feeds), citing Reuters and Ian King/Bloomberg. dedup-check before opening: no match.

claims.text: SK Group and Nvidia signed letters of intent on 24 July 2026 for a partnership the companies describe as worth more than $500 billion, covering AI factory construction and next-generation memory supply
claims.reasoning: Confirmed via direct fetch of Nvidia's own newsroom press release (joint SK Group/Nvidia announcement, quotes from both Jensen Huang and Chey Tae-won), independently corroborated by HotHardware's own reporting (byline Paul Lilly, 2026-07-25) which adds its own framing/context rather than only repeating the release. An adversarial search pass found one secondary blog claiming 'no official press release... had emerged' -- resolved as stale/incorrect since the Nvidia newsroom release itself was directly fetched and confirms the figure.

claims.text: SK Telecom plans to build a 2-gigawatt AI factory in South Korea on Nvidia's DSX architecture, using Nvidia Vera Rubin compute with SK hynix HBM4 memory, targeting the first phase online in 2027
claims.reasoning: Stated identically in both the Nvidia newsroom release and HotHardware's independent writeup.

claims.text: SK hynix and Nvidia agreed to a separate long-term partnership to secure HBM supply for Nvidia and jointly develop next-generation AI memory
claims.reasoning: Confirmed in both sources; explicitly framed as letters of intent, not a signed final supply contract -- reflected in the article body rather than treating the deal as fully closed.

falsifier_notes: Verdict: CLEAR TO PUBLISH, with caveats reflected in the article. Adversarial search surfaced market-side skepticism (SK hynix shares down ~41% from peak same week) but this concerns earnings/valuation sentiment, not the veracity of the deal terms themselves -- not evidence against the claims. Also surfaced that the arrangement is letters of intent rather than binding final contracts; the headline and body were written to reflect that explicitly rather than imply a closed deal. CNBC's own piece could not be fetched (403); not used as evidence load-bearing beyond confirming the same headline figure independently in search snippets.
